lede: Monday's Town Council meeting is the one to watch this week — they're voting on whether to convert two affordable ownership units at 215 East Colorado Avenue into employee dwelling units with no maximum sale price, a structural change to how that housing works for the community. The School Board's monthly meeting tackles second-reading votes on board policies and resolutions backing Proposition NN and Amendment 87, while the County Commissioners continue a public hearing on adopting new statewide building codes that will shape construction across the valley for years.

notable.stake: Board votes on Prop NN, Amendment 87 resolutions and two revised policies.
Resolution could remove price cap on two affordable ownership units, changing their status permanently.
Council votes on deed-restriction conversion removing sale-price cap from two affordable units.
Commission weighing new leak-check fee and six leak-forgiveness requests affecting ratepayers.
Continued public hearing on new building codes that set construction standards countywide.
Early review of school-district employee housing project and ongoing land-use discussion — public eyes needed.
